questions.prompt: What is the charge of an electron?
questions.explanation: An electron has a negative charge.

questions.prompt: Which pair of particles is found in the nucleus of an atom?
questions.explanation: Protons and neutrons are in the nucleus; electrons are around it.

questions.prompt: A neutral atom contains 6 protons and 7 neutrons. How many electrons does it contain?
questions.explanation: A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons. Neutrons have no charge.

questions.prompt: Two oxygen atoms are chemically joined. What do they form?
questions.explanation: The atoms form a molecule, but both atoms are oxygen, so it is a molecule of an element.

questions.prompt: Water contains hydrogen and oxygen chemically combined. How is water classified?
questions.explanation: A compound contains different elements chemically combined.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest particle of an element?
questions.explanation: An atom is the smallest particle of an element.

questions.prompt: Which value is used to arrange elements in increasing order in the Periodic Table?
questions.explanation: The ordering principle taught in the notes is increasing proton number.

questions.prompt: Where are most metals found in the Periodic Table?

options.A: On the left and in the centre

questions.explanation: Most metals occupy the left and central regions.

questions.prompt: Hydrogen is placed on the left of the Periodic Table. What type of element is it?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen is a non-metal even though it is placed on the left.

questions.prompt: Why is a systematically arranged Periodic Table useful?

options.A: It makes every element behave in the same way.
options.B: It helps us find and compare elements.
options.D: It shows only elements used in jewellery.

questions.explanation: Systematic arrangement helps us locate elements and compare them.

questions.prompt: Which pair of properties makes copper suitable for electrical wires?

options.B: Dull and a poor electrical conductor
options.D: Ductile and a good electrical conductor

questions.explanation: Copper can be formed into wires and allows electricity to pass through it.

questions.prompt: In the conductivity test, the ammeter needle deflects when a carbon rod is connected. What does this show?

options.A: The carbon rod must be a metal.
options.D: The carbon rod has become a metal.

questions.explanation: Needle deflection indicates current. The carbon used in this experiment conducts electricity despite being a non-metal.

questions.prompt: What is the charge of a proton?
questions.explanation: A proton is positively charged.

questions.prompt: What is the charge of a neutron?
questions.explanation: A neutron has no electrical charge; it is not negatively charged.

questions.prompt: Which type of element is found in the far-right column of the Periodic Table?
questions.explanation: The notes place inert gases, including helium, neon and argon, at the far right.

questions.prompt: Which two elements combine to form polythene?
questions.explanation: The approved notes list carbon and hydrogen as the elements in polythene.

questions.prompt: Silicon has characteristics of both metals and non-metals. How is silicon classified?
questions.explanation: Silicon is a semi-metal, with characteristics of both metals and non-metals.

questions.prompt: Which element has the symbol Fe?
questions.explanation: The notes give Fe as the chemical symbol for iron.

questions.prompt: What property allows a material to be hammered into sheets?
questions.explanation: Malleability means the ability to be hammered into sheets.

questions.prompt: In the electrical-conductivity test, what property of the rods should be kept the same?
questions.explanation: The type of material is changed, while the size of the material is kept constant.

questions.prompt: A manufacturer needs a lightweight cooking pot that transfers heat efficiently. Which combination of properties is most suitable?

options.A: High density and poor heat conductivity
options.B: Low density and good heat conductivity
options.C: Low density and poor heat conductivity
options.D: High density and good heat conductivity

questions.explanation: Low density keeps the pot lightweight, while good heat conductivity allows heat to transfer efficiently.

questions.prompt: A solid element is not attracted to a magnet. A pupil concludes that it must be a non-metal. Which statement best evaluates this conclusion?

options.A: It is reliable because magnetism distinguishes every metal from every non-metal.
options.B: It is reliable if the same result is obtained three times.
options.C: It is unreliable because some metals, such as aluminium, are non-magnetic.
options.D: It is unreliable only because the sample’s mass was not measured.

questions.explanation: Some metals, including aluminium, are non-magnetic. A lack of magnetic attraction does not establish that an element is a non-metal.

questions.prompt:
Three rods of equal length and thickness are heated separately under the same conditions. Identical thumbtacks are attached at the same distance from the heated ends using equal amounts of wax.

Time taken for each thumbtack to fall:
P: 20 seconds
Q: 45 seconds
R: 75 seconds

Which conclusion is supported by the results?

options.A: P transfers heat to the wax fastest.
options.B: R is the best heat conductor.
options.C: P has the lowest melting point.
options.D: All three rods conduct heat equally well because their dimensions are identical.

questions.explanation: The thumbtack on P falls first, showing that heat reaches and melts its wax fastest under the same test conditions.

questions.prompt: A metal wire must support a heavy load without breaking. Which property is most important?
questions.explanation: Tensile strength describes a material’s ability to withstand a pulling force without breaking.

questions.prompt: A pupil compares the melting points of two substances. What quantity should she measure when each substance melts?
questions.explanation: A melting point is the temperature at which a substance melts.
